1. Introduction

This manual defines operational standards for the Atlas platform. All personnel must follow these guidelines to ensure consistency, safety, and quality across deployments.

Updates are published quarterly and distributed through the internal change management system. Review the revision history at the end of this document for the latest amendments.

Scope
All engineering, operations, and support teams.
Audience
Operators, engineers, managers, auditors.
Version
4.2.1
Effective
2025-01-15

2. Purpose

The purpose of this manual is to codify repeatable processes that reduce variance and improve reliability. Each section contains actionable steps, examples, and verification criteria.

Teams should treat this document as the single source of truth. Where conflicts arise between this manual and local runbooks, the manual takes precedence unless formally exempted.

Objective
Standardize operations.
Metric
Mean time to recovery.
Target
Under 15 minutes.
Review
Quarterly.

3. Scope

Scope covers all production services, staging environments, disaster recovery procedures, and incident response protocols managed by the Atlas organization.

Exclusions include third-party vendor-specific configurations that do not affect core service availability. Such items are documented in separate vendor annexes.

Included
Core services, pipelines, monitoring.
Excluded
Vendor hardware specifics.
Boundary
Customer-facing APIs.
Review
Annual.

4. Definitions

Definitions establish a common vocabulary. Terms used throughout this manual are defined here to eliminate ambiguity and ensure consistent interpretation across teams.

If a term is not listed, consult the central glossary repository. Propose additions via the change request process.

Service
A deployable unit with a defined SLA.
Incident
An unplanned interruption to a service.
Change
A modification to production infrastructure.
Audit
A formal review of compliance.

5. Roles and Responsibilities

Clear role definitions prevent gaps during incidents and changes. Each role has specific duties, escalation paths, and required competencies.

Personnel may hold multiple roles, but accountability must remain unambiguous. Document role assignments in the central registry.

Incident Commander
Leads response and coordination.
On-call Engineer
Executes remediation steps.
Communications Lead
Manages stakeholder updates.
Auditor
Verifies compliance post-event.

6. Change Management

All changes to production must follow the change management process. This includes code deployments, configuration updates, infrastructure modifications, and database schema changes.

Changes are classified as standard, normal, or emergency. Each classification has distinct approval requirements and implementation windows.

Standard
Pre-approved, low risk.
Normal
Requires CAB approval.
Emergency
Expedited approval path.
Post-change
Verification within 30 minutes.

7. Incident Response

Incident response procedures ensure timely detection, reporting, classification, and resolution of service disruptions. The process is triggered automatically by monitoring alerts or manually by user reports.

Severity levels range from SEV-5 (informational) to SEV-1 (critical). Response times and escalation thresholds are defined per severity.

Detection
Automated monitoring or user report.
Triage
Assign severity and owner.
Resolution
Remediate and verify.
Review
Post-incident within 48 hours.

8. Monitoring

Monitoring covers infrastructure health, application performance, security events, and business metrics. Alerts are routed to on-call personnel via paging and chat integrations.

Dashboards are maintained by the observability team. SLOs are reviewed monthly and adjusted based on capacity and risk tolerance.

Latency
p95 under 200ms.
Error rate
Below 0.1%.
Availability
99.95% monthly.
Capacity
Headroom above 30%.

9. Backup and Recovery

Backup policies define frequency, retention, and verification procedures. Recovery time objectives and recovery point objectives are agreed upon with business stakeholders.

Test restores are performed quarterly. Backup integrity is verified using checksums and spot checks.

Frequency
Hourly incremental, daily full.
Retention
30 days online, 1 year archive.
RTO
4 hours.
RPO
15 minutes.

10. Security

Security policies protect confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data and systems. All personnel must complete annual security training and adhere to least privilege principles.

Vulnerability scanning runs weekly. Penetration testing occurs semi-annually. Findings are tracked to remediation.

Authentication
MFA required for all accounts.
Encryption
TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest.
Auditing
Immutable logs retained 1 year.
Incident
Report within 1 hour of discovery.

11. Access Control

Access to systems is granted based on role and necessity. Privileged access is time-bound and requires dual approval. Reviews occur quarterly.

Service accounts are rotated every 90 days. Break-glass procedures exist for emergency scenarios.

RBAC
Role-based access control.
MFA
Mandatory for all users.
Review
Quarterly recertification.
Rotation
90 days for service accounts.

12. Configuration Management

Configuration items are stored in version control. Changes follow the change management process. Drift detection runs hourly and alerts on unauthorized modifications.

Secrets are managed via a dedicated vault. Rotation policies are enforced automatically.

Repository
Git with signed commits.
Drift
Hourly automated checks.
Secrets
Vault with 90-day rotation.
Audit
Immutable change log.

13. Deployment

Deployments use immutable infrastructure. Releases are packaged as artifacts and promoted through environments. Canary and blue-green strategies reduce risk.

Rollbacks must be automated and tested. Deployment windows are scheduled to minimize user impact.

Strategy
Canary then full rollout.
Artifact
Signed container image.
Rollback
Automated within 5 minutes.
Window
02:00-04:00 UTC.

14. Testing

Testing includes unit, integration, contract, performance, and security tests. All code must pass automated pipelines before promotion.

Test coverage targets are 80% line and 75% branch. Performance budgets are enforced in CI.

Unit
Per function or method.
Integration
Service interactions.
Performance
Load and stress tests.
Security
SAST and DAST scans.

15. Documentation

Documentation is maintained alongside code. API references, runbooks, and architecture diagrams are stored in the central wiki and linked from service repositories.

Documentation changes undergo the same review process as code. Stale documentation is flagged automatically.

OpenAPI 3.0 spec.
Runbook
Step-by-step procedures.
Diagram
UML or C4 model.
Review
Quarterly freshness check.

16. Training

All new hires complete onboarding within two weeks. Ongoing training includes quarterly security briefings and annual certification renewals.

Specialized training is required for on-call and incident commander roles. Completion is tracked in the learning management system.

Two weeks mandatory.
Security
Quarterly briefing.
Certification
Annual renewal.
Tracking
LMS integration.

17. Compliance

Compliance obligations include GDPR, SOC 2, and PCI DSS where applicable. Evidence is collected continuously and reviewed by internal audit.

Non-compliance findings trigger remediation plans with defined deadlines. Exceptions require executive approval.

GDPR
Data protection.
SOC 2
Trust services criteria.
PCI DSS
Payment data security.
Audit
Annual external review.

18. Risk Management

Risks are identified, assessed, and mitigated. The risk register is reviewed monthly. High risks require mitigation plans and owner assignments.

Risk appetite is defined by the executive committee. Acceptable residual risk levels are documented per service.

Likelihood
Probability scale 1-5.
Impact
Business impact scale 1-5.
Mitigation
Action to reduce risk.
Owner
Accountable individual.

19. Vendor Management

Vendors are evaluated for security, reliability, and support. Contracts include SLAs, audit rights, and termination clauses.

Vendor performance is reviewed quarterly. Critical vendors have contingency plans.

Evaluation
Security and reliability review.
SLA
Uptime and response commitments.
Audit
Right to audit annually.
Contingency
Failover plan required.

20. Capacity Planning

Capacity planning ensures resources meet demand with acceptable performance. Forecasting uses historical trends and business projections.

Scaling policies are automated where possible. Thresholds trigger alerts and auto-scaling actions.

12-month rolling average.
Headroom
30% minimum.
Scaling
Automated with manual override.
Review
Monthly.

21. Service Catalog

The service catalog lists all production services with descriptions, owners, SLAs, and dependencies. It is the authoritative source for service inventory.

Services are classified by criticality. Tier-1 services have the highest availability requirements and fastest response times.

Catalog
Central registry of services.
Owner
accountable team.
SLA
Agreed availability target.
Dependency
Upstream and downstream links.
